# Agentplane egress

> Discover your ServiceAccount's effective outbound access and credential presentation without obtaining real credentials.

Use the Egress rules base URL from your platform instructions. Fetch `GET /v1/rules` through the
configured proxy with `Authorization: Bearer agentplane-credential-agentplane-workload`
(`agentplane egress rules` does this and prints the same response with `--json`).
The response names your authenticated `subject` and effective policies. Their rules provide `hosts`,
`methods` and `paths` (each a `values` list, or `null` for any), and any `credential`'s identity,
description, exact placeholder, and presentation `targets`. A rule whose `credential` is `null`
allows access without substituting one. An empty `policies` list means no egress.

PolicySets can bundle egress, Action auto-approval and Kubernetes rules; PolicyBindings attach them
to a ServiceAccount and may expire. The live rules describe effective egress, not every available
grant. A Session ID, launch preset, or credential name does not establish access.

Preserve the configured proxy and CA trust. Send exact placeholders in their declared presentation;
never obtain substituted tokens, bypass the proxy, or disable certificate verification. A placeholder
is inert outside the substitution path. Prefer existing allowed credentials, standing Kubernetes
permissions, or auto-approved Actions before requesting an Action that needs manual approval.

## Workflows

- [Credentials and refusals](/docs/agents/credentials.md): Read before using an unfamiliar credential or diagnosing a failed proxied call.

## Discovery

- [Effective rules](/v1/rules): Your current destinations, request scopes, credential identities, and presentation targets.
